hints: Identify class boundaries by extending each integer interval by 0.5: 100.5 to 120.5, 120.5 to 130.5, 130.5 to 135.5, 135.5 to 145.5, 145.5 to 160.5.
Compute frequency density = frequency / class width for each class: 18/20 = 0.9, 48/10 = 4.8, 34/5 = 6.8, 32/10 = 3.2, 18/15 = 1.2.
Draw histogram bars on a linear scale with correctly labelled axes.
walkthrough:
Calculate class boundaries, widths, and frequency densities:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Class} & \text{Boundaries} & \text{Width} & \text{Frequency } (f) & \text{Frequency Density } (\text{fd} = f / w) \\ \hline 101 - 120 & 100.5 - 120.5 & 20 & 18 & 18 / 20 = 0.9 \\ 121 - 130 & 120.5 - 130.5 & 10 & 48 & 48 / 10 = 4.8 \\ 131 - 135 & 130.5 - 135.5 & 5 & 34 & 34 / 5 = 6.8 \\ 136 - 145 & 135.5 - 145.5 & 10 & 32 & 32 / 10 = 3.2 \\ 146 - 160 & 145.5 - 160.5 & 15 & 18 & 18 / 15 = 1.2 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Construct the histogram:
- Horizontal axis: Time in minutes, scaled linearly from $100$ to $160$.
- Vertical axis: Frequency density, scaled linearly from $0$ to at least $7$.
- Draw contiguous rectangular bars matching the calculated boundaries and heights.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Understand why frequency density must be used:
Because the classes have unequal widths ($20, 10, 5, 10, 15$), bar heights in a histogram must represent frequency density, where $\text{Area} = \text{Frequency}$.

Step 2: Find the exact class boundaries:
Times are recorded to the nearest minute, so each class begins $0.5$ below the lower integer and ends $0.5$ above the upper integer:
- $101 - 120 \implies [100.5, 120.5]$, width $= 20$
- $121 - 130 \implies [120.5, 130.5]$, width $= 10$
- $131 - 135 \implies [130.5, 135.5]$, width $= 5$
- $136 - 145 \implies [135.5, 145.5]$, width $= 10$
- $146 - 160 \implies [145.5, 160.5]$, width $= 15$

Step 3: Calculate the frequency density for each bar:
$$\text{Frequency density} = \frac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class width}}$$
- Bar 1: $\frac{18}{20} = 0.9$
- Bar 2: $\frac{48}{10} = 4.8$
- Bar 3: $\frac{34}{5} = 6.8$
- Bar 4: $\frac{32}{10} = 3.2$
- Bar 5: $\frac{18}{15} = 1.2$

Step 4: Draw the histogram:
- Label the vertical axis 'Frequency density'.
- Label the horizontal axis 'Time (minutes)'.
- Draw the 5 adjacent bars with correct widths and heights on linear scales.

hints: Find the midpoints of the 5 classes: 110.5, 125.5, 133.0, 140.5, 153.0.
Calculate sum(f * x^2) = 2630272.5, find variance = 2630272.5 / 150 - (131.9)^2 = 137.54, then standard deviation = sqrt(137.54) = 11.7 minutes.
walkthrough:
Calculate the estimated mean $\bar{x}$:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{\sum f x}{\sum f} = \frac{19785}{150} = 131.9\text{ minutes}$$

Calculate the estimated variance and standard deviation:
$$\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum f x^2}{\sum f} - \bar{x}^2 = \frac{2630272.5}{150} - (131.9)^2 = 17535.15 - 17397.61 = 137.54$$
$$\sigma = \sqrt{137.54} \approx 11.7277 \approx 11.7\text{ minutes}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the midpoint $x$ of each class interval:
$$\text{Midpoint} = \frac{\text{Lower boundary} + \text{Upper boundary}}{2}$$
- Class 1: $\frac{100.5 + 120.5}{2} = 110.5$
- Class 2: $\frac{120.5 + 130.5}{2} = 125.5$
- Class 3: $\frac{130.5 + 135.5}{2} = 133.0$
- Class 4: $\frac{135.5 + 145.5}{2} = 140.5$
- Class 5: $\frac{145.5 + 160.5}{2} = 153.0$

Step 3: Compute the estimated mean:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{\sum f x}{n} = \frac{19785}{150} = 131.9\text{ minutes}$$

Step 5: Compute the estimated variance:
$$\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum f x^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2 = \frac{2630272.5}{150} - (131.9)^2 = 17535.15 - 17397.61 = 137.54$$

Step 6: Compute the standard deviation:
$$\sigma = \sqrt{137.54} \approx 11.727745$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $11.7$ minutes.
